pass_a_gloss: And it is likely that we will also be insulted by people living near and jeered at by some ringing us round and moving the head at us as over senseless people. But when these things come about, let us say toward God: you placed us as an insult to those living near us, a jeering and laughter to those in a circle round us; you placed us into a proverb among the gentiles, a moving of head among the peoples; the whole day my turning in shame is opposite me, and the disgrace of my face covered me over, from a voice of one insulting and speaking against, from the face of a foe and one chasing out. And it is a happy thing, also over all these things coming about, to say to God the voice from frankness of the prophet carried on after them: all these things came upon us, and we did not let you slip from memory, and we did not do wrong in your covenant, and our heart did not stand away into the things behind.
pass_b_english: It is likely that we will also be reproached by our neighbours and sneered at by some who surround us and shake their heads at us as at fools. But when this happens, let us say to God: “You have made us a reproach to our neighbours, a sneer and a laughingstock to those around us. You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me, at the voice of the one who reproaches and slanders, at the sight of the enemy and the persecutor” (Psalm 44:13-16). And it is a blessed thing, even as all these things are happening, to say to God the words which the prophet, out of his boldness, adds to them: “All these things have come upon us, and we have not forgotten you, and we have not been false to your covenant, and our heart has not turned back” (Psalm 44:17-18).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 19); the old English was a digest. The old English invented a taunt ('Where is your God? ...') and a quotation of 1 Peter 4:14 tagged as Psalm 44:13, and dropped most of Psalm 44:13-16.
Read ὑπὸ γειτόνων ('by neighbours'), the M reading recorded in Koetschau's apparatus.
®g read ὡς; uaxapıov read μακάριον; 00x read οὐκ; ἢ ἐντροπή read ἡ ἐντροπή.
Greek Psalm 43:14-19 is English Psalm 44:13-18; the quotation runs to the first half of 44:18 ('our heart has not turned back').
